thread:
Praveen Rao: Alert from OpsBot — unusual KMS decrypt spike for projects/redwood-prod at ~2026-03-20T12:03:00Z, ~1200 decrypts/min from svc-account:llm-ingest-sa. Saw an RBAC change at 11:55 UTC (audit entry).
OpsBot: [ALERT] k8s-prometheus: high_kms_decrypt_rate detected on project=redwood-prod resource=kms.googleapis.com key=projects/redwood-prod/locations/us/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/llm-key
Amanda Chen: Copy. Confirming: was there a deliberate rollout earlier? @Sara @Liam
Sara Velasquez: We pushed an RBAC binding change at 11:54 for a quick test (granted roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter to platform:ingest-role). I thought it was limited to staging — investigating if prod got included.
Liam O'Neill: I can pull the audit logs now. Running:
```
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloudkms_key" protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND timestamp>="2026-03-20T11:50:00Z"' --project=redwood-prod --limit=50
```
Liam O'Neill: First pass: 85% of decrypts from svc-account:llm-ingest-sa, other 15% from service:router@redwood-prod. Many requests have large payloads (embedding feature).
Praveen Rao: Impact: expensive tokenise/embedding pipeline potentially leaking extra usage. Need containment: revoke the RBAC change and disable the ingest SA keys. @Sara can you revert the binding and remove roles for the SA now?
Sara Velasquez: Reverting RBAC binding now. Command used:
```
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member='serviceAccount:platform-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter'
```
Sara Velasquez: Rolled back at 12:10 UTC. Note: existing session tokens may still be valid for a short window.
Amanda Chen: Good. Next step: rotate the KMS key and revoke access tokens for the affected SA. Liam — can you block the SA from calling KMS via deny policy or remove SA keys?
Liam O'Neill: Creating an IAM deny policy for that SA on the cryptoKey resource now. Also listing service account keys:
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=platform-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-prod
```
Liam O'Neill: Found one user-managed key — disabling it now:
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable <key-id> --iam-account=platform-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
Praveen Rao: Start KMS key rotation plan too — create a new key version and switch production to new version after validation. Sara, please own the rotation and create a short rollback plan.
Sara Velasquez: Creating new cryptoKeyVersion now. Will schedule cutover to new key version in 30m after smoke tests. Also exporting audit log slice to GCS for forensics:
```
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloudkms_key" timestamp>="2026-03-20T11:50:00Z"' --project=redwood-prod --format=json > /tmp/kms-audit-20260320.json
gsutil cp /tmp/kms-audit-20260320.json gs://redwood-incident-archive/1901234567/
```
Amanda Chen: Notification: paging SRE oncall to throttle embeddings endpoint until we confirm no backfill or retries causing the spike. @Liam can you add a rate limit on router -> embeddings config (temporary)?
Liam O'Neill: Pushed a temporary rate-limit flag on the ingress router (10 req/s per SA) at 12:21 UTC. Monitoring.
OpsBot: [INFO] rate_limit_change applied by Liam O'Neill at 12:21:40Z
Praveen Rao: Evidence collection checklist:
- snapshot KMS audit logs (Sara)
- revoke SA keys (Liam)
- rollback RBAC changes (Sara) ✅
- throttle embeddings traffic (Liam) ✅
- start postmortem ticket INC-2026-279 and assign
Amanda Chen: I'm setting up the incident page and handoff notes. Current severity: P2 (cost + potential data access). No confirmed data exfil yet.
Sara Velasquez: Forensics note: there are ~2400 decrypts between 11:55 and 12:15. Most decode calls have identical payload shape -> likely automated job. Adding user-agent and origin info to the artifact bucket.
Praveen Rao: Next actions before handoff: Sara finish rotation and upload audit slice; Liam confirm SA keys disabled and rate-limits holding; Amanda prepare comms for legal/PR if needed. I'll be on-call until 12:45 UTC then hand off to Amanda.
Amanda Chen: Acknowledged. I'll take over at 12:45 UTC. Interim summary for next shift:
- What happened: accidental RBAC mis-scope allowed ingest SA to decrypt prod KMS key; caused high decrypt volume and cost spike.
- Actions taken: RBAC reverted, SA keys disabled, temporary rate limits, KMS key rotation initiated, audit logs archived.
- Open items: validate that no consumer cached the old key, finish full key rotation, update least-privilege RBAC policy, run job backfill check.
Amanda Chen: Handoff ticket: INC-2026-279, assigned to Amanda Chen (owner) / Sara Velasquez (forensics) / Liam O'Neill (mitigation). Notes pinned in incident doc: https://redwood.company/inbox/INC-2026-279
Liam O'Neill: Confirmed: SA keys disabled and deny policy applied at 12:33 UTC. Rate limiting holding; decrypt rate down to baseline.
Sara Velasquez: Audit slice uploaded to gs://redwood-incident-archive/1901234567/kms-audit.json. Rotation completed and new key version in use at 12:39 UTC.
Praveen Rao: Thanks team. Amanda — please run the post-incident review focusing on RBAC deployment tooling to avoid prod bleed-through. Assign to devex + infra.
Amanda Chen: Will do. Closing warroom at 12:48 UTC. Final note: keep INC-2026-279 open until final postmortem and RBAC playbook updates are complete. :white_check_mark:
